item.title: Antenna Spotting
item.description: One of my new hobbies is what I call antenna spotting: walking around and identifying real communications antennas in the wild.

item.title: Quantum RF Sensing
item.description: In this post I work through the question: can a quantum RF receiver replace my traditional receiver? I had a perfect excuse to answer it. I was building a downlink for the GOES-R geosynchronous weather satellite, and the link budget was tight enough to make any noise-floor improvement worth chasing. So I looked hard at Rydberg-atom receivers, did the math, and came away with a nuanced answer. This post walks you through what I found, with equations, scaling laws, and a couple of scripts you can run yourself.

item.title: Parabolic Dish Antenna Basics
item.description: If you plan to dive into a Radio Frequency (RF) project, getting familiar with a few core antenna types is essential. Choosing or designing the right antenna is one of the most fundamental skills in electrical engineering, and understanding the first principles behind them will help you move quickly from concept to a working system that transmits and receives reliably.

item.title: Deep Learning with Radio Frequency Signals
item.description: Signal Classification Using Spectrograms and Deep Learning In this post, I will introduce some basic methods for utilizing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to process spectrograms created from Radio Frequency (RF) data. The information in the post was taken from a tutorial my colleagues and I provided to NVidia Corporation in early 2015 that has been used in their enterprise training series for several years. This post links you to a git project that removes the dependency on Nvidia’s DIGITS platform and uses only Keras and Tensorflow. Project Code & Data
